title: Charts modeled on the sharp characteristic of a log regular scheme
statement: Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $\bar x$ be a geometric point above $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $P=\overline M_{\bar x}$. Then $P$ is a finitely generated integral saturated sharp monoid (sharp means that $0$ is its only invertible element), and there is a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)\to(X,\bar x)$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, def-weil-etale-morphism] with a chart $P\to M|_W$ whose induced map $P\to\overline M_{\bar w}$ is the chosen identification with $P$. The chart may be taken on an affine locally Noetherian $W$.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.6, printed p. 70: P is fs sharp and X admits a chart modeled on P at the geometric point (before the completed-local-ring formulas).

proof.text: By the fs-chart definition, choose an etale-local chart $Q\to M$ through $\bar x$ with $Q$ fine saturated. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and let $F\subseteq Q$ be the inverse image of $A^\times$. It is a face: in a commutative ring a product is a unit exactly when both factors are units, since an inverse to $ab$ gives inverses $b(ab)^{-1}$ and $a(ab)^{-1}$ to $a$ and $b$. The chart definition gives $M_{\bar x}=Q\oplus_F A^\times$. Inverting $F$ changes nothing in this pushout, since every element of $F$ already maps to a unit. Thus $M_{\bar x}=Q_F\oplus_{F^{\rm gp}}A^\times$. Quotienting this presentation by $A^\times$ identifies the given characteristic $P$ with $Q_F/F^{\rm gp}$, with the map induced by the original chart.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1 and 1.6, printed pp. 69--70; explicit stalk pushout calculation.

proof.text: Apply the face-sharpening lemma to $Q,F$. It gives that $P=Q_F/F^{\rm gp}$ is finitely generated, integral, saturated and sharp, and that $P^{\rm gp}=Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}$ is free of finite rank. It also gives $(Q_F)^\times=F^{\rm gp}$. These conclusions require saturation of $Q$; no ordinary regularity of $X$ is used.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.6 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 70 and 75; Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.5.

proof.text: Choose a finite basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $P^{\rm gp}$ and, for each $e_i$, choose a lift $a_i\in Q^{\rm gp}$ through the quotient. Define $s(\sum_i n_ie_i)=\sum_i n_ia_i$ for integers $n_i$. Uniqueness of the basis expression makes $s$ a group homomorphism and the quotient composed with $s$ is the identity. For $p\in P$ choose $q\in Q_F$ representing $p$. Then $s(p)-q\in F^{\rm gp}$, which is the unit group of $Q_F$. Hence $s(p)\in Q_F$. This constructs a monoid section $s|_P:P\to Q_F$. In fact $(p,f)\mapsto s(p)+f$ is an isomorphism $P\oplus F^{\rm gp}\to Q_F$: its inverse sends $q$ to $(\bar q,q-s(\bar q))$, whose second component belongs to $F^{\rm gp}$. Both composites are identities by these formulas.

source.place: Expose VI, 3.7(a), printed p. 75: choose a splitting of (3.a); explicit nonequivariant basis construction.

proof.text: Push this isomorphism out along $F^{\rm gp}\to A^\times$. The formulas give an isomorphism $P\oplus A^\times\to M_{\bar x}$ sending $(p,u)$ to $h(p)u$, where $h$ is $s|_P$ followed by $Q_F\to M_{\bar x}$. On the quotient by units the map induced by $h$ is the identity of the specified $P$. Its inverse image of $A^\times$ is therefore $\{0\}$: a germ mapping to a ring unit lies in the unit subgroup of the log structure, and $P$ is sharp. Consequently the log structure associated to the prelog map $P\to A$ is exactly $P\oplus A^\times$, and the displayed map is the stalk logification isomorphism required for chart spreading.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 69 and 75; explicit associated-log-stalk calculation.

proof.text: Apply the fine-log stalk-chart spreading lemma to $h$. The source monoid is fine by step 2 and the required logification isomorphism was proved in step 4. It produces an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $W$ and a chart with precisely this germ. Its characteristic map at $\bar w$ is consequently the chosen identification with $P$, not an unspecified automorphism. Finally $W\to X$ is locally of finite presentation by the etale definition. Its affine algebra presentations have finitely many generators, so it is locally of finite type. As $X$ is locally Noetherian, apply the locally-Noetherian finite-type lemma (Stacks Tag 01T6, morphisms-lemma-finite-type-noetherian) to conclude that $W$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Expose VI, 3.7(a), printed p. 75, final sentence; Stacks Project, Tag 01T6, morphisms-lemma-finite-type-noetherian for local Noetherianity.

proof_origin.place: Expose VI, 1.6 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 70 and 75: explicit nonequivariant splitting argument with its monoid and chart-spreading inputs isolated.

Step 1: the fs chart Q, F = preimage of A^x is a face, M_x = Q_F (+)_{F^gp} A^x, so P = Q_F/F^gp; this matches the chart formula in def-trf-fs-log-blowup. Step 2: the face-sharpening lemma applies with these hypotheses. Step 3: the basis-lift section lands in Q_F because F^gp is the unit group of Q_F, and Q_F = P (+) F^gp. Step 4: the composite to the characteristic is the identity, so E = {0} and the stalk iso is exactly the spreading node's hypothesis. Step 5: spreading gives an affine W with germ h; etale implies lfp, then lft, then 01T6 (Mathlib leaf; tool_use accepted). I proved every clause of lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening by hand: Q_F finitely generated and saturated, units = F^gp, R sharp, fs and embedded, R^gp torsion-free hence free. Small cases N^r, Z/n and N+Z/n all behave correctly. lem-trf-fine-log-stalk-chart-spreading is the standard Kato/Ogus fine-chart spreading fact; it is true and strictly smaller than the item because the germ is given.
